text: Which mechanism allows bacteria to perform temporal comparisons when navigating chemical gradients?
choices: Spatial comparison across their cell body length
Temporal comparison of receptor occupancy over time while swimming
Receptor clustering at the leading edge only
explanation: Bacteria are too small to measure a gradient spatially across their body. Instead, they perform temporal comparisons: while tumbling and running, they compare current receptor occupancy to a short-term memory of recent occupancy encoded in methylation state of chemoreceptors. This allows directed migration up attractant gradients.
